subject: Capacity mediation: Brightline pilot reservation plan
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity mediation: Brightline pilot reservation plan

Morning team —

Brightline confirmed their pilot scope yesterday (6k concurrent inference tokens/min peak, ~50k embeddings/day) and asked for a short reservation to guarantee stable latency during the 4-week pilot (start target: 2027-06-07). They want a committed lane between 9am–6pm PT weekdays with burst to production if needed.

Questions I want aligned on before I respond:
- Can we carve a 2x small-GPU slice (equivalent to 2 A30 slots) in a Dedicated pool for the pilot window?
- If we grant a weekday occupancy window, what autoscale override (if any) do we need to allow Brightline to burst beyond the reserved slice for critical runs?
- Any compliance/privileged routing notes we should include for their contract team?

I’ll attach the initial SOW in a follow-up but want product + infra sign-off on the reservation posture and the fallback path (fallback: route to hosted Canary model at slightly higher latency).

Thanks —
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: brightline_sow_stub.txt (text)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity mediation: Brightline pilot reservation plan

+1 on the ask. Quick posture and proposal below — see draft MOP attached.

Proposal (short pilot-run):
- Reserved lane: 2x small-GPU equivalent (2x A30 slots) in Dedicated pool-us-west for pilot duration 2027-06-07 -> 2027-07-04.
- Window: 0900–1800 PT weekdays (reduce daytime contention).
- Burst: soft burst allowed up to 4x slots for up to 30m per day via autoscale-exception flag (manual approval from operations on first burst). After first week, if telemetry looks stable, set autoscale-exception to automated with a 5m rate-limit cooldown.
- Fallback: route to hosted-cpu-capable model (canary) if Dedicated queue >60s for >2 minutes.

Operational requirements:
- Telemetry: token-level latency traces and per-request model variant tags.
- Cost: estimate ~ $6.4k for the 4-week reserved window + expected burst usage (rough ballpark).
- Security: put their traffic on tenant-isolated VPC route; no additional encryption requirements beyond KMS.

I attached a one-page MOP (brightline_mop_draft.pdf) that operations can follow. If we all agree, I’ll create the reservation ticket and pre-allocate the slice.

-Kim
Director, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachment: brightline_mop_draft.pdf (pdf)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity mediation: Brightline pilot reservation plan

Thanks Kim — this reads reasonable and conservative. A couple of follow-ups before we confirm with Brightline procurement:

1) Autoscale exception lifecycle: prefer we do manual approval for the first 48 hours of the pilot (not just first burst). Ops, please keep a 2-hr SLA to acknowledge manual burst approvals in the first 48 hours. After day 3, we can flip to the automated 5m cooldown approach that Kim suggested.

2) Cost framing: Aditya, can you give the buyer a simple monthly equivalent for their procurement doc (one-line $ figure + note that burst will be billed at on-demand rates)? We should avoid giving a large variance range.

3) PO/Contract logistics: Markus, please confirm whether procurement needs a DocuSign placeholder for the reservation (we can attach the MOP + SOW).

If everyone agrees to the above, I’ll reply to Brightline with the operational guardrails and a small checklist (PO, start date confirmation, and telemetry hooks).

—Naomi
Head of Customer Success, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Note: forwarding the MOP to Brightline ops to indicate pre-allocation planning.
From: Brightline Procurement <procurement@brightline.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity mediation: Brightline pilot reservation plan

Naomi / Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement confirmed they can issue a PO for the 4-week pilot. Attached is our PO draft (brightline_po_v1.pdf) and a requested DocuSign template (link in-line).

Two items from our side:
- Start date: we prefer 2027-06-14 (shifted one week) to align with our internal compliance checks — open to earlier if you can confirm telemetry hooks.
- Burst policy: procurement asked that any manual approval required for burst be handled by one named contact on Redwood side (we will need a response within 2 business hours otherwise the system will default to decline). Can you provide that contact?

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/r/redwood-brightline/placeholder

Best,
Amira Hassan
Procurement Manager
Brightline Health

Attachment: brightline_po_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity mediation: Brightline pilot reservation plan

Summarizing next steps (agreeing to Naomi + Kim):
- Naomi to confirm the weekday window and manual-approval SLA with Brightline (Naomi to reply to Amira).
- Aditya will send a one-line cost figure ($6,400 for the 4-week reserved lane + on-demand burst rates) and confirm billing cadence.
- Kim / Ops to open a reservation ticket with the ops playbook attached and mark autoscale-exception flag as manual-only for first 48 hours.
- I will generate a DocuSign placeholder and add the MOP as an exhibit (Procurement, please confirm the legal contact if you want specific contract language).

If no objections, I’ll mark this as green and we can move to reservation.

-Markus
VP, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
